data.why: New feature with a new notifier component across the CLI and tracker, and channel and event choices that need a PRD

data.subject: decision-alerts
data.ask: Q1 Channel: where should a decision alert appear?
data.why: macOS desktop alerts reach you away from the terminal and browser with no server running; browser alerts work only while the cockpit tab is open
data.costOfWaiting: DA-01.1 and DA-01.2 wait; browser or both adds a browser feature

data.subject: decision-alerts
data.ask: Q2 Events: which events should send an alert?
data.why: Stale approvals, late updates and decisions older than 2 working days are only found when gates are read, so they need a timed check, and timed reminders are a non-goal

data.subject: decision-alerts
data.ask: Q3 Limits: one alert per decision with macOS Focus, or our own rate limit and quiet hours?
data.why: You already control Focus; decisions per hour is UNKNOWN, so our own limit needs numbers only you can give

data.subject: decision-alerts
data.ask: Q4 Systems: macOS only, or also Linux and Windows?
data.why: The agents run on your Mac; Linux and Windows support is UNKNOWN. Other systems send nothing and never fail the command

data.subject: decision-alerts
data.ask: Q5 Record: where should each sent alert be recorded?
data.why: An alert is a fact about one Mac; the committed event log is shared history every clone merges, and test runs would add to it. Cost: the coverage metric is measurable only on your Mac
data.costOfWaiting: DA-04.1, DA-04.2 and the first success metric wait

data.subject: decision-alerts
data.ask: The QA testability check cannot run before the PRD gate (spawn guard EN-10.1 needs a build-ready task). How should we proceed?
data.why: Each of the 17 criteria already has a written test note; QA maps every criterion to a test at the QA stage anyway. Fixing devolps is a separate change in another repo
data.costOfWaiting: The PRD gate request waits; nothing else is blocked

data.subject: decision-alerts
data.ask: Who adds the line /.project-notify/ to the root .gitignore? No role can write .gitignore today.
data.why: devops-sre already owns repository config (package.json, tsconfig.json), and T1 must merge first anyway. Only you edit .claude/.
options: devops-sre adds it in task T1; you add .gitignore to devops-sre's write scope in .claude/harness.json
You add the line by hand in the T1 pull request
Drop the root line; rely only on the folder's own .gitignore that the CLI writes
data.recommendation: devops-sre adds it in task T1; you add .gitignore to devops-sre's write scope in .claude/harness.json
data.costOfWaiting: T1 and T2 cannot be built as designed until this is answered; the design gate is not blocked.

data.subject: 2026-w42
data.override: Quick-track CI has no analyze step; specs/ci/quick.md lists its one task and a check for every requirement

data.title: Rollback misses the required status check on master
data.detail: The PM decided (card c-a5d4fd) to make ci a required check on master. Once set, disabling or deleting the workflow leaves every pull request waiting for a check that never comes, so GitHub blocks every merge, including the one that deletes the workflow. Fix: first rollback step removes ci from the required checks; correct the closing lines. PR #8 code review, finding 1.

data.findingId: 465bf2e:docs/runbooks/ci.md:46:The failing step is not the last one sho
data.title: The failing step is not the last one shown
data.detail: GitHub lists skipped steps and the Post Run and Complete job steps after the failure. Fix: say to find the step with the red X; later steps show as skipped. PR #8 code review, finding 2.

data.findingId: 465bf2e:docs/runbooks/ci.md:54:npm test builds the tools first, so buil
data.title: npm test builds the tools first, so build errors show in step 3
data.detail: scripts/run-tests.mjs line 32 builds the tools before tests, so an esbuild error fails npm test with no test name. Fix: add one sentence to the npm test bullet. PR #8 code review, finding 3.

data.title: No timeout-minutes on the ci job
data.detail: GitHub's default is 360 minutes. A hung test keeps ci pending for up to 6 hours and holds the sprint's merge chain. The first run took about 1 min 40 s. Fix: timeout-minutes: 15 on the job. PR #8 code review, finding 4.

data.title: Checkout leaves its token on disk
data.detail: No step needs git credentials, so pull request code has no reason to see the token. Impact is small: the token can only read a public repository. Fix: persist-credentials: false on the checkout step. PR #8 code review, finding 5 (optional hardening).

data.subject: 2026-w42
data.ask: 5 tool-call counter events (run.progress, no decisions) were logged on master after the PR 8 merge and are now in a git stash. Restoring them needs a hand merge of the tracker log, which EN-07.5 forbids. Drop them, or keep the stash?
data.why: They only count this session's tool calls; every decision and gate event is already restored and committed.
data.costOfWaiting: None to the sprint. The stash only waits in the local clone.

data.findingId: f1222f2:docs/runbooks/ci.md:39:Runbook says tests never send notificati
data.title: Runbook says tests never send notifications; the requirement is never show
data.detail: DA-03.2 says running the tests never shows notifications to the PM. After da-t2 and da-t3 the notify suite sends to a stub notifier on purpose, so 'never send' becomes wrong. Fix: 'so tests never show a real notification.' PR #10 code review, L1. (L2, the feat(tests) commit type, has no file line; it is fixed by squash-merging with the PR title.)

data.findingId: f1222f2:docs/runbooks/ci.md:40:Runbook overstates TH-19: a suite with a
data.title: Runbook overstates TH-19: a suite with a fresh env does not get the switch
data.detail: 'so tests never send notifications' is stronger than TH-19's residual: a suite that builds a child's environment from scratch does not get the off switch. Fix: 'do not send real notifications. A suite that starts a child process must spread process.env into its env.' PR #10 security review, F3 (optional). Fixed together with code-review L1.
